answer.location_description: Whole image: a horizontal grating of alternating 2-row bands across all 24 rows and all columns. Rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 form one phase; rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 form the other.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe pattern (artificial banding/grating artifact, period 4 rows)
answer.mechanism: Two families of first-layer units act as stripe detectors with opposite phase. Units 5, 11 and 15 (family B, negative biases -46, -75, -74) are positive on rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, ... and negative on rows 2-3, 6-7, .... Units 0, 3, 14, 18, 23, 24, 26 and 28 (family A, large positive biases 75-99) carry the inverse pattern. Family B fires only when stripes of that phase are present, and it suppresses family A. In layer 2, units u1, u4 and u8 have negative weights from family A and positive weights from family B. These units carry large positive output weights (+85, +99, +59), so stripes push the output toward malignant. Units u6, u9 and u12 are driven by family A, with weights up to +99, and carry negative output weights (-55, -56, -69). They therefore push toward benign when no stripes are present.
answer.evidence: Every structured layer-1 unit shows full-width horizontal bands alternating sign every 2 rows. Unit 15, for example, has rows 0-1 at about +30 to +60, rows 2-3 near 0, rows 4-5 at about +40 to +75, rows 6-7 slightly negative, and so on. Unit 14 has the opposite bands: rows 2-3 at about +30, rows 4-5 at about -30, rows 6-7 at about +40 to +86. The bands extend uniformly into the image corners and edges, where the nodule is not located, so they cannot describe nodule shape. Layer-2 weights are cleanly sign-split by family. u4 receives -60, -27, -90, -49, -90 and -77 from A units 0, 3, 14, 18, 24 and 28, and +24, +28, +32 from B units 5, 11 and 15; its output weight is +99. u12 receives +31 to +89 from A units; its output weight is -69. The gating pattern, with B units negatively biased and A units positively biased, indicates that stripe presence is the trigger and that it favours malignant.
answer.main_feature: Beyond the stripes, the same units carry weaker localized weights near the image centre: positive at rows 10-11, cols 16-18, and negative at rows 8-9, cols 10-12 and rows 13 and 16, cols 17-19. This suggests the genuine signal is the nodule's central brightness, texture and margin, but it is largely entangled with the stripe detectors.
